'''William Gonzales Padolina''' (born November 15, 1946) is a Filipino chemist who served as Secretary of the [[Department of Science and Technology (Philippines)|Department of Science and Technology]] of the [[Philippines]].

==Early life and education==
William Gonzales Padolina was born on November 15, 1946, in [[Pasay]] (then part of [[Rizal (province)|Rizal]]). He graduated with a degree in [[agricultural chemistry]] from the [[University of the Philippines Los Baños]] in 1968 and a doctorate degree from the [[University of Texas at Austin]] in 1973.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last1=Toledo |first1=Adel Castillo |title=DR. WILLIAM G. PADOLINA: Humanity first before science |url=https://www.philstar.com/business/business-as-usual/2005/11/21/307785/dr-william-g-padolina-humanity-first-science |work=Philstar.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Kay |first=Benjamin |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Who_s_who_in_Asia_and_the_Pacific_Nation/Qq4UAQAAIAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&bsq=William+Padolina&dq=William+Padolina&printsec=frontcover |title=Who's who in Asia and the Pacific Nations |last2=Bootman |first2=Cara |date=1999 |publisher=International Biographical Centre |isbn=978-0-948875-63-2 |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==
Padolina was president of the [[National Academy of Science and Technology]]. He is a professor and academician.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A Labor Market Analysis of S&T Human Resource Needs in the Philippines (Available on Facebook Live) |url=http://www.pids.gov.ph/details/event/a-labor-market-analysis-of-s-t-human-resource-needs-in-the-philippines-available-on-facebook-live |access-date=2026-02-28 |website=www.pids.gov.ph |language=en-US}}</ref>

He was [[Secretary of Science and Technology (Philippines)]] from July 7, 1994, to January 29, 1999.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Parnala |first=Adam |date=2022-08-21 |title=LIST: All the DOST Secretaries in the Philippines |url=https://www.noypigeeks.com/government/dost-secretaries/ |access-date=2026-02-28 |website=NoypiGeeks |language=en-US}}</ref>

Padolina's tenure included the PHNET project, which connected the Philippines to the [[internet]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Evangelista |first=Paeng |title=Ateneans connect to the world |url=https://www.philstar.com/business/technology/2014/04/14/1312233/ateneans-connect-world |access-date=2026-02-28 |website=Philstar.com}}</ref> and the Magna Carta for science and technology workers, which increased benefits to discourage leaving for higher-pay abroad.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Weathermen, S&T workers buck removal of benefits |url=https://www.philstar.com/metro/2016/01/25/1546366/weathermen-st-workers-buck-removal-benefits |access-date=2026-02-28 |website=Philstar.com}}</ref>
